advances: Identifies a uniform obstruction to every admissible partial buffer on a ternary base box and proves that a heavy occupied-rank-at-most-two slice on this class already supplies the curvature branch, with loss at most 9/4. An explicit family of actual coupled convex bodies has no such buffer, has vanishing normalized low-rank slice scores, and nevertheless has the accepted curvature and mixed-depth certificates despite unbounded curvature. A separate box family shows that concentration of the actual partial marginal does not force a heavy low-rank slice in the original mixed measure. These are geometric restrictions and successful examples for the proposed three-way alternative, not a disproof of it or a resolution of the unrestricted locked conjecture.

proof:
First establish the counting fact used for both families. Let \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a finite nonempty set whose affine hull has dimension \(k\), and put \(V:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(A-A)\). The restrictions of the \(n\) coordinate functionals span \(V^*\): a vector of \(V\) annihilated by all of them is zero. Choose \(k\) of these restrictions forming a basis. The resulting projection onto those \(k\) original coordinates is injective on \(V\), hence on \(\operatorname{aff}(A)\). If each original coordinate of \(A\) takes at most \(s\) values, injectivity gives \(|A|\le s^k\). For \(k=0\), the nonempty affine hull is a singleton and the bound is \(|A|=1=s^0\). In particular, every affine-rank-\(k\) subset of \(\{0,1,2\}^n\) has at most \(3^k\) elements. The proof imposes no coordinate alignment or primitivity assumption on its affine hull.

For the buffer obstruction, fix arbitrary \(U,q,r\) and put
\[
B_U:=U^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}0_{q\times r}\\I_r\end{pmatrix}
\in\mathbb Z^{n\times r}.
\]
Unimodularity makes \(U^{-1}\) integral, and \(B_U\) has rank \(r\ge1\). Suppose \(P\) has the stated projected cube. Since its retained coordinates are zero, the original base projection of \(F_U^{-1}(P)\) contains \(B_U\mathbf a+RB_U[-1,1]^r\). Every point of this latter set is realized: a rounded coordinate in the projected cube has a preimage in \(P\), whose base pulls back by \(U^{-1}\). Consequently the original base projection of \(\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}F_U^{-1}(P)\) contains
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}B_U\mathbf a+\frac32B_U[-1,1]^r,
\]
because \(\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}R=3/2\). The width of this set in original coordinate \(i\), meaning its maximum minus its minimum in that coordinate, is \(3\sum_{l=1}^r|(B_U)_{il}|\). Some row of the positive-rank integer matrix is nonzero, so at least one such width is at least three.

If a nonempty \(E\) satisfied \(E+\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}P\subseteq F_U(C)\), fix \(e\in E\) and apply the linear inverse \(F_U^{-1}\). This would place a translate of \(\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}F_U^{-1}(P)\) inside \(C\). Its base projection would then have every original coordinate width at most two, since the base projection of \(C\) is contained in \([0,2]^n\). This contradicts the preceding width bound. The argument holds for every \(U,P,R,q\) under the interface's exact coordinate convention, and it uses no ratio, symmetry, or origin-containment assumption on \(P\). Integer translations of the base coordinates would not alter this width obstruction either.

Still under the ternary-box hypothesis, \(D_+\subseteq\{0,1,2\}^n\). Apply the counting fact to \(A=D_+\cap\Sigma\), whose affine dimension is exactly \(q_\Sigma\). At most \(3^{q_\Sigma}\) positive original fibers contribute, each with weight at most \(M_w\), proving \(W_\Sigma\le3^{q_\Sigma}M_w\). The zero displacement at any positive center has \(\Delta_j(0)=0\) and \(\alpha_j(0)=w_j\), so \(B_j^\Delta(0)\ge w_j\). Taking a maximizing fiber gives \(K(w)\ge M_w\). Therefore
\[
\frac{2^{n-q_\Sigma}W_\Sigma}{W}
\le\left(\frac32\right)^{q_\Sigma}\frac{2^nM_w}{W}
\le\frac94\frac{2^nK(w)}{W}
\qquad(0\le q_\Sigma\le2).
\]
Taking the supremum proves the score comparison. Alternatively, directly combining the assumed heavy-slice inequality with the counting bound gives
\[
K(w)\ge M_w\ge a\left(\frac23\right)^{q_\Sigma}2^{-n}W
\ge\frac{4a}{9}2^{-n}W.
\]
This establishes assertion 1 and its equivalence up to absolute constants: the buffer branch is absent, the heavy-slice branch implies the curvature branch with constant reduced by at most \(4/9\), and the curvature branch itself already suffices for the disjunction. No uniform curvature assertion for arbitrary ternary-box bodies is assumed here.

Consider next \(C_n\). Each function \(z\mapsto(z_i-1)_+\) is convex and nondecreasing in its coordinate, and each \(c_i\) is positive. Thus \(\phi\) is convex and coordinatewise nondecreasing. The constraints \(x_k+\phi(z)/(4n)\le1\), together with the box and nonnegativity constraints, define a convex closed set. Since
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n c_i=n+\frac{n(n+1)}{2(n+1)}=\frac{3n}{2},
\]
every \(z\in[0,2]^n\) has \(0\le\phi(z)\le3n/2\), so its fiber side length lies in \([5/8,1]\). In particular \(x=0\) realizes every base point, proving the exact base projection. The set is bounded and contains the open set \((0,2)^n\times(0,5/8)^n\), so it is compact and full-dimensional.

The only possible integer base coordinates are ternary. On those coordinates, \((z_i-1)_+\) is one precisely when \(z_i=2\), and is zero otherwise. The continuous fiber is exactly the product of \(n\) intervals of the stated common side length, proving the displayed weight formula. Every such weight is positive. Coordinatewise increases can only increase \(\phi\), proving the required monotonicity. Every weight is at most one, and every \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\) has weight one; hence \(M_w=1\).

To verify actual coupling, fix distinct \(i,j\) and write \(a_i:=c_i/(4n)\) and \(a_j:=c_j/(4n)\) within this calculation. Both are positive and their sum is less than one. At the four ternary points \(0,2e_i,2e_j,2e_i+2e_j\), the formula yields
\[
w_{2e_i+2e_j}w_0=(1-a_i-a_j)^n
<\bigl((1-a_i)(1-a_j)\bigr)^n
=w_{2e_i}w_{2e_j}.
\]
The strict inequality follows from \((1-a_i)(1-a_j)=1-a_i-a_j+a_ia_j>1-a_i-a_j>0\). A product of one-coordinate weights would satisfy equality in this rectangle identity. Such a factorization is therefore impossible.

If a ternary point has \(k\) coordinates equal to two, the inequality \(c_i<2\) gives \(w_z\ge(1-k/(2n))^n\). The concave function \(u\mapsto\log(1-u/2)\) on \([0,1]\) lies above its chord between the endpoints. Thus \(\log(1-u/2)\ge-u\log2\); take \(u=k/n\) and exponentiate to obtain \((1-k/(2n))^n\ge2^{-k}\). There are exactly \(\binom nk2^{n-k}\) ternary points with precisely \(k\) twos, because every other coordinate independently equals zero or one. Consequently
\[
W\ge\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk2^{n-k}2^{-k}
=\left(2+\frac12\right)^n
=\left(\frac52\right)^n.
\]
Assertion 1 excludes every partial buffer. Its counting estimate, together with \(M_w=1\), gives for every positive slice of occupied rank at most two
\[
\frac{2^{n-q_\Sigma}W_\Sigma}{W}
\le\frac{2^{n-q_\Sigma}3^{q_\Sigma}}{(5/2)^n}
=\left(\frac32\right)^{q_\Sigma}\left(\frac45\right)^n
\le\frac94\left(\frac45\right)^n.
\]
This bound is uniform over all primitive slices and tends to zero, proving the asserted eventual failure for each fixed positive threshold.

All hypotheses of accepted fact c13fd517ed177886 have now been verified directly for this actual body: its base dimension is the present \(n\), its continuous dimension is the present \(d=n\), its body is \(C_n\), its positive integer weights are supported on the ternary cube, those weights are coordinatewise nonincreasing, and \(W>0\). In its scalar clause use \(\widetilde w_z=w_z\) and \(\widetilde W=W\). At each center its \(\widetilde\alpha(v),\widetilde{\mathcal U}_j,\widetilde\Delta_j(v),\widetilde B_j^\Delta(L)\) then become respectively the present \(\alpha_j(v),\mathcal U_j,\Delta_j(v),B_j^\Delta(L)\), with identical orientation and zero-displacement conventions. Its largest-block conclusion gives \(K(w)\ge(3\,7^{2/3})^{-1}2^{-n}W\), and its actual-body conclusion gives the single point \(p_n^\star\) and halfspace lower bound stated above. The strict comparisons with the constants \(1/11\) and \(\ell/176\) follow from \((3\,7^{2/3})^3=1323<1331=11^3\). The point is selected before every halfspace, exactly as in that accepted theorem; no scalar-table depth conclusion without actual-body realization is used.

Finally \(w_{\mathbf1}=w_{\mathbf0}=1\) and \(w_{2\mathbf1}=(1-(3n/2)/(4n))^n=(5/8)^n\). Both endpoints have positive weight. Substitution into the same curvature definition from 280b299bc1e87c14 gives \(\Delta_{\mathbf1}(\mathbf1)=\log(1/(5/8)^n)=n\log(8/5)\), which tends to infinity. This completes assertion 2.

For assertion 3, \(\widehat C_N\) is a product of nondegenerate compact intervals for every integer \(N\ge1\), hence a convex body. Retaining its first coordinate, its four-dimensional section volume is
\[
g_N(\eta)=
\begin{cases}
2(2N)^3,&0\le\eta\le1,\\
0,&\eta\notin[0,1].
\end{cases}
\]
There are exactly two nonzero integer samples, at zero and one, so \(M_N=2(2N)^3\), \(G_N=4(2N)^3\), and \(M_N/G_N=1/2\). These are volumes in the three continuous rounded coordinates and the one original continuous coordinate. For the original mixed measure, the full positive lattice support is instead \(\{0,1\}\times\{-N,-N+1,\ldots,N\}^3\), containing exactly \(2(2N+1)^3\) points, each with continuous fiber \([-1,1]\) of length two. Hence \(W_N=4(2N+1)^3\), with no change of measure implicit in either count.

Every original coordinate of this finite support takes at most \(2N+1\) values, since \(2\le2N+1\). Apply the proved coordinate-injection bound to its positive points in any slice of occupied rank \(q_{N,\Sigma}\). It gives at most \((2N+1)^{q_{N,\Sigma}}\) such points, so \(W_{N,\Sigma}\le2(2N+1)^{q_{N,\Sigma}}\). For \(0\le q_{N,\Sigma}\le2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2^{4-q_{N,\Sigma}}W_{N,\Sigma}}{W_N}
&\le2^{3-q_{N,\Sigma}}(2N+1)^{q_{N,\Sigma}-3}\\
&=\frac{2}{2N+1}
\left(\frac{2}{2N+1}\right)^{2-q_{N,\Sigma}}
\le\frac{2}{2N+1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is a bound in the original fiber measure, uniform over every primitive slice, even when its lattice rank exceeds its occupied rank. It tends to zero although the partial-marginal peak ratio remains one half.

For completeness the buffer on this family is explicit. Set
\[
P_N:=\{0\}\times[-N,N]^3\times\{0\},
\qquad
K_N:=[0,1]\times\{0\}^3\times[-1,1].
\]
Then \(\widehat C_N=K_N+P_N\). In the genuine-summand clause of 8444e75361af26b0 take its \(C,K,P,q,r,d,R,k\) to be respectively \(\widehat C_N,K_N,P_N,1,3,1,N,3\). In particular its \(K\) is the compact summand \(K_N\), not the curvature score \(K(w)\). For \(N\ge4\), define \(E_N:=K_N+(1-3/(2N))P_N\), a convex body since its three rounded side lengths \(2N-3\) are positive. It satisfies \(E_N+\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}P_N=\widehat C_N\), and \(P_N\) has the required radius-\(N\) rounded projection. Directly counting the same two retained integer sections gives
\[
\frac{\mu_1(E_N)}{\mu_1(\widehat C_N+\beta_{\mathrm{buf}}P_N)}
=\frac{4(2N-3)^3}{4(2N+1)^3}
=\left(\frac{2N-3}{2N+1}\right)^3
\ge\frac18=2^{-3},
\]
with positive denominator. The last inequality holds because \((2N-3)/(2N+1)\ge1/2\) whenever \(N\ge7/2\). This verifies the actual ratio and containment required by the accepted interface, completing assertion 3.
statement:
Let \(n\ge3\) and \(d\ge1\) be integers, and let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body with \(W>0\). Use the actual-body objects of accepted fact 280b299bc1e87c14: for \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(C_z:=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}\) and \(w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)\); let \(W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z\), \(S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\), and \(h_S(p):=\inf_{H\ni p}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), over closed ambient halfspaces. Empty and lower-dimensional fibers have weight zero. Put \(D_+:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:w_z>0\}\) and \(M_w:=\max_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z\).

For \(j\in D_+\), set \(\alpha_j(v):=\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\}\), \(\mathcal U_j:=\{v\in\mathbb Z^n:\alpha_j(v)>0\}\), and \(\Delta_j(v):=\log(w_j^2/(w_{j+v}w_{j-v}))\) on \(\mathcal U_j\), using natural logarithms. Define the curvature-cutoff score by
\[
B_j^\Delta(L):=\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j\\\Delta_j(v)\le L}}\alpha_j(v),
\qquad
K(w):=\max_{\substack{j\in D_+\\L\ge0}}\frac{B_j^\Delta(L)}{1+L}.
\]
Here \(\alpha_j(v)\) is exactly the predecessor's \(\alpha(v)\) at center \(j\), and \(K(w)\) is exactly its final cutoff maximum. Displacement sums are oriented and count zero once. The predecessor proves that actual-body curvature is nonnegative and this maximum is attained.

A primitive affine lattice slice is a set \(\Sigma=z_0+\Gamma\), where \(z_0\in\mathbb Z^n\) and \(\Gamma\le\mathbb Z^n\) is saturated, meaning \(\Gamma=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(\Gamma)\cap\mathbb Z^n\). Its original fiber mass is \(W_\Sigma:=\sum_{z\in\Sigma}w_z\). When \(W_\Sigma>0\), its occupied intrinsic rank is \(q_\Sigma:=\dim\operatorname{aff}(D_+\cap\Sigma)\); this can be smaller than the rank of \(\Gamma\). Rank zero is permitted. Empty positive-fiber slices have mass zero and are omitted from score suprema.

The partial buffers in this statement are exactly those of accepted fact 8444e75361af26b0. More explicitly, choose \(U\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)\), let \(F_U(z,x):=(Uz,x)\), choose \(q\in\{1,2\}\), and put \(r:=n-q\). In the transformed coordinates write \((\eta,t,x)\in\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^d\). A buffer is a nonempty compact convex set \(P\subseteq\{0_q\}\times\mathbb R^{r+d}\) for which \(\mathbf a+R[-1,1]^r\subseteq\pi_r(P)\) for some \(\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^r\) and \(R>0\), where \(\pi_r\) is projection onto \(t\). Set \(\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}:=3/(2R)\) and \(\beta_{\mathrm{buf}}:=1/(2R)\); these are respectively \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) in 8444e75361af26b0, distinct from the reflected weights \(\alpha_j(v)\). Admissibility requires a convex body \(E\) with \(E+\alpha_{\mathrm{buf}}P\subseteq F_U(C)\). The partial measure is \(\mu_q(A):=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^q}\operatorname{vol}_{r+d}(A_j)\), computed in this chosen split, exactly as in that predecessor. A positive ratio requirement concerns \(\mu_q(E)/\mu_q(F_U(C)+\beta_{\mathrm{buf}}P)\), with positive denominator.

The following conclusions hold.

Assertion 1. If the base projection of \(C\) is contained in \([0,2]^n\), there is no admissible partial buffer for any \(U\), either \(q\), or any \(R>0\). In fact the containment fails even if \(E\) is allowed to be an arbitrary nonempty set, without any ratio requirement. Every positive-mass primitive slice with \(q_\Sigma\le2\) satisfies
\[
W_\Sigma\le3^{q_\Sigma}M_w,
\qquad
\sup_{\substack{\Sigma\text{ primitive},\ W_\Sigma>0\\q_\Sigma\le2}}
\frac{2^{n-q_\Sigma}W_\Sigma}{W}
\le\frac94\frac{2^nK(w)}{W}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(a>0\), a slice satisfying \(W_\Sigma\ge a\,2^{-(n-q_\Sigma)}W\) forces \(K(w)\ge(4a/9)2^{-n}W\). On this ternary-box class, a uniform buffer-or-heavy-slice-or-curvature alternative is therefore equivalent up to absolute constants to its curvature assertion alone.

Assertion 2. For every integer \(n\ge3\), set \(d=n\), \(c_i:=1+i/(n+1)\), and \(\phi(z):=\sum_{i=1}^n c_i(z_i-1)_+\), where \(u_+:=\max\{u,0\}\). Define
\[
C_n:=\left\{(z,x):z\in[0,2]^n,\quad
0\le x_k\le1-\frac{\phi(z)}{4n}\quad(1\le k\le n)\right\}.
\]
This is a compact full-dimensional convex body with base projection exactly \([0,2]^n\). In the definitions above take \(C=C_n\). Its actual integer fiber weights are
\[
w_z=\left(1-\frac{\sum_{i:z_i=2}c_i}{4n}\right)^n
\quad(z\in\{0,1,2\}^n),
\qquad
w_z=0\quad(z\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0,1,2\}^n).
\]
All ternary weights are positive, the table is coordinatewise nonincreasing on the ternary cube, \(M_w=1\), and it cannot be written as a product of one-coordinate weights. Moreover, \(W\ge(5/2)^n\). Every admissible partial buffer is impossible in every unimodular base coordinate system, and
\[
\sup_{\substack{\Sigma\text{ primitive},\ W_\Sigma>0\\q_\Sigma\le2}}
\frac{2^{n-q_\Sigma}W_\Sigma}{W}
\le\frac94\left(\frac45\right)^n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus for every fixed \(a>0\), all sufficiently large members of this family fail the heavy-slice requirement with that constant. Nevertheless accepted fact c13fd517ed177886 applies and gives
\[
K(w)\ge\frac{1}{3\,7^{2/3}}2^{-n}W
>\frac1{11}2^{-n}W.
\]
Writing \(\ell:=-\log(1-e^{-1})\), it also gives one \(p_n^\star\in C_n\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^n)\) such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing it satisfies
\[
\mathcal H_n\bigl(C_n\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^n)\cap H\bigr)
\ge\frac{\ell}{48\,7^{2/3}}2^{-n}W
>\frac{\ell}{176}2^{-n}W.
\]
At the positive center \(j=\mathbf1\) and displacement \(v=\mathbf1\), the curvature is \(\Delta_{\mathbf1}(\mathbf1)=n\log(8/5)\). In particular these successful cutoff examples do not have a dimension-independent bound on all their reflected curvatures.

Assertion 3. For the separate family with fixed \(n=4,d=1\), use the distinct notation
\(\widehat C_N:=[0,1]\times[-N,N]^3\times[-1,1]\) for integers \(N\ge1\). This is the rectangular family denoted \(C_N\) in the supplied first response, distinguished here from the coupled family \(C_n\). Retain the first base coordinate \(\eta\), put
\(g_N(\eta):=\operatorname{vol}_4\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R:(\eta,t,x)\in\widehat C_N\}\),
\(G_N:=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}g_N(j)\), and \(M_N:=\max_{j\in\mathbb Z}g_N(j)\).
Then \(M_N/G_N=1/2\), whereas its original mixed volume is \(W_N=4(2N+1)^3\). For every positive-mass primitive slice, with \(W_{N,\Sigma}\) and \(q_{N,\Sigma}\) defined from this body's original positive fibers as above,
\[
q_{N,\Sigma}\le2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\frac{2^{4-q_{N,\Sigma}}W_{N,\Sigma}}{W_N}
\le\frac{2}{2N+1}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus failure of the condition \(M_N\le G_N/12\) does not force a heavy occupied-rank-at-most-two slice at any fixed positive normalized threshold. For \(N\ge4\), this family does have an admissible buffer with \(q=1\) and partial ratio at least \(2^{-3}\), in accordance with the genuine-summand interface of 8444e75361af26b0.
